quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift down one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, move down one gear at a time. Slowly release the clutch through the friction zone between each gear change.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in a crash.

questions.question: When it is obvious that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need to use a turn signal at traffic lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Other vehicles you cannot see may be nearby. Signals are always necessary.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting.
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a common way to slow down a motorcycle. Note that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing whenever you ride. Crashes happen in daylight and at night, so wear highly visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the most effective action you can take to survive a crash.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before and explain everything.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before and explain everything.
questions.explanation: Passengers need to understand how to stay safe on a motorcycle. Never assume they know what to do. Give clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: If only one alcoholic drink is consumed:

options.text: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on the body.
The effect on the body only lasts a short time.
Coffee can remove the alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol from your system.

questions.question: When riding in a group:

options.text: The group should be as large as possible.
Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leaders.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind. Keep groups small to stay together and avoid blocking traffic. Pairing up blocks riders' escape routes.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: It will handle the same as your own bike.
The lender will check the brakes for you.
Keep extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep extra space between you and other vehicles to give yourself more time to react.
questions.explanation: Check your borrowed motorcycle the same way you check your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike and keep extra space when you need to stop.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol may still affect you.
questions.explanation: Your body removes one drink of alcohol per hour on average. However, alcohol can build up in your body. Your abilities and judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Bright colors make you easier to see. Wear clothes that stand out during the day and night.

questions.question: When choosing footwear, pick:

options.text: Shoes with long laces you can't tuck in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Keep heels short so they don't catch. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is enough.
Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A low tire may still look normal, so you can't rely on looking at it.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash:

options.text: Keep other drivers guessing about what you will do.
Always stay one foot away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Be visible at all times. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show other drivers your plans. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use strong, durable materials.

questions.question: Most motorcycles:

options.text: Have a front brake and a rear brake.
Have three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass other vehicles.
A motorcycle cannot pass other vehicles.
A motorcycle can pass if no other vehicle is coming.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass other vehicles.
questions.explanation: No passing zones prohibit all passing. You also cannot pass by riding off the road.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Limits your movement in the lane.
Lets you rely on others to find hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, like all vehicles.
You should make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, like all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Like any vehicle, a motorcycle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of wearing riding gloves?

options.text: Don't wear them because they make your hands too hot.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
Don't wear them because they make controls harder to use.
Wear them only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or other durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride in the lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What is a benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance?

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will continue to run like new. Regular maintenance and inspections keep your motorcycle in good condition.

questions.question: Which sign is typically rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular and white with black lettering. Follow the rules posted on these signs.
